subject: Draft: damage-tiering & definition compromise — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Annette Cho <acho@acmeinc.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME MSA redlines — damages section review

Evelyn,

Attached is ACME's consolidated redline (v3) for the MSA and the Order Form. Key flag from legal: they will not accept a mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages. Their position is that the exclusion must be one-way (customer cannot recover consequential damages from vendor) but allow carve-outs for IP indemnity, gross negligence, and data breach.

They also tightened the definition of "consequential/special/incidental" to include any downstream lost profits, loss of business, and third-party claims arising from ACME's downstream customers. They've left the cap language tied to fees for 12 months.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept: (1) one-way exclusion with the three carve-outs above, and (2) preserve the 12-month fees cap? If not, please propose narrow compromise language.

Attachments: ACME_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf (PDF, 23KB); OrderForm_ACME_2027-05.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

Thanks,
Annette
Annette Cho
Senior Counsel, ACME, Inc.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Annette Cho <acho@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines — damages section review

Annette — thanks for the consolidated redline and the clear ask. We're aligned on wanting to move quickly. Two quick notes from our side: 

1) Mutuality: Redwood's standard is to propose mutual exclusions for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages, with narrowly tailored carve-outs for IP indemnity, data breach, and willful misconduct. Mutuality is important for risk symmetry — it limits exposure for both parties and is something we typically insist on for enterprise deals.

2) Cap interplay: Tying a cap to 12 months of fees is common, but we need to ensure the carve-outs (IP, data breach, willful misconduct) are uncapped. ACME's proposed one-way exclusion + 12-month cap would create asymmetry where Redwood retains exposure for the same categories ACME carved out — that is a hard sell to execs.

Proposed compromise language (drafted for your counsel's review):
"Except for (a) claims for infringement or misappropriation of the other party's intellectual property, (b) either party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or (c) unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data, neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, indirect, incidental, punitive or exemplary damages arising out of this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the aggregate liability of either party for claims not excluded above shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."

This keeps the exclusion mutual, preserves the 12-month cap for non-excluded claims, and leaves the three carve-outs uncapped.

If ACME cannot accept mutuality, Redwood can consider a one-way exclusion but only if the one-way carve-outs are strictly limited and we obtain an explicit data-breach indemnity (or cap carve-out) and a reciprocal limitation for Redwood on consequential losses caused by ACME's downstream integrations.

Propose a short call tomorrow to talk through options — cc'ing Rishi and Karthik from legal/negotiations.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_Damage_Language.txt (inline)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ACME MSA redlines — damages section review

Adding a few points from legal/ops perspective: 
- If we push for mutuality, we should add a short illustrative list in the definition of "consequential/special/incidental" to reduce ambiguity (e.g., "including, without limitation, lost profits, loss of business, loss of data use, third-party claims for downstream customers"). Concrete examples reduce future disputes.
- For data breach carve-out: we should require Customer to notify within 7 days and cooperate; we can accept an uncapped carve-out for actual regulatory fines and direct remediation costs, but insist that third-party consequential claims remain capped (unless willful misconduct).
- Keep the cap tied to 12 months of fees, but add a cross-reference that Order Form surcharges (e.g., reserved capacity credits) are included in the calculation so the cap reflects committed spend.

If we go one-way, we must get explicit indemnity for data incidents caused by ACME (i.e., when ACME's failure causes a breach of our environment) and walk through a carve-out matrix.

Rishi
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Bradley King <bking@acmeinc.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Annette Cho <acho@acmeinc.com>, Procurement - ACME <procurement@acmeinc.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ACME MSA redlines — damages section review

Evelyn — appreciate the suggested language, but ACME's position remains that the exclusion must be one-way and they will not agree to mutuality. Their counter proposal is below (excerpt):

---- EXCERPT START ----
"Vendor shall not be liable for consequential, special, incidental, or punitive damages arising out of or related to this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section does not limit Customer's rights with respect to: (i) claims for infringement of Customer's intellectual property; (ii) Customer's direct damages resulting from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct; or (iii) damages related to unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor. Vendor's aggregate liability for direct damages shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) $500,000."
---- EXCERPT END ----

ACME rejects uncapped carve-outs and will not accept mutual language. The additional $500k floor on the cap is their hedge. They also pushed the scope of consequential to explicitly include "losses to third-party customers" which they expect us to accept as a vendor risk.

We are happy to take a short call with Redwood counsel to iron out the remaining language — procurement would like to keep momentum.

Bradley King
Counsel, ACME, Inc.
[Attachment: ACME_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf referenced inline]

Thanks all — summary and next steps: 
1) Options for Redwood: 
   a) Stand firm on mutual exclusion with uncapped carve-outs for IP, data breach, willful misconduct + 12-month fee cap for other claims.
   b) Accept ACME one-way exclusion only if ACME narrows carve-outs (no blanket third-party downstream carve-out), accepts a data-breach indemnity, or agrees to a $X minimum cap and explicit limits on third-party pass-through losses.
2) Ask ACME to clarify whether the $500k floor in their excerpt applies in addition to the 12-month fee cap (their excerpt suggests OR $500k). If so, that materially changes economics for larger accounts.
3) Propose a 30-minute legal call Thursday 10:00am PT to agree on carve-out matrix and whether a mutual middle-ground is possible. 

Evelyn/Rishi: if you want, I'll draft two redline alternatives (mutual compromise and one-way with strict carve-out matrix) and circulate before the call.

Karthik
Head of Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
